newsitem.title: USA: Dry weather saps soil moisture in Oklahoma.
newsitem.headline: Dry weather saps soil moisture in Oklahoma.

text.p: Dry weather sapped soil moisture in the week ended Sunday, leaving subsoil ratings at the lower point so far this year, the agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"Dry weather coupled with high temperatures has sapped soil moisture levels and caused stress-related problems to some crops," the report said. "Subsoil moisture has dwindled to the lowest level of 1997."
Corn ratings deteriorated from last week as heat stressed the crop during pollination. The crop was rated 55 percent good to excellent, down from 94 percent last week.
Corn was tasseling on 57 percent of the acreage, below the five-year average of 91 percent. None of the crop was mature, against five percent average.

Sorghum ratings also dropped as the crop showed signs of heat and moisture stress. The crop was rated 12 percent poor, 23 percent fair, 60 percent good and five percent excellent. The crop was 15 percent headed, against 29 percent average.

Topsoil moisture was rated six percent very short, 44 percent short, 46 percent adequate and four percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was rated three percent very short, 19 percent short, 73 percent adequate and five percent surplus.
